item.title: SCMP: Has AI solved the Riemann hypothesis? Claim makes waves at 200th birthday event in China
item.description: A US-based mathematician has stunned the community by claiming to have solved the nearly 170-year-old Riemann hypothesis using artificial intelligence (AI). The news broke on Friday as a major conference opened in southern China’s Shenzhen, where world-leading mathematicians have gathered until Monday to mark the 200th anniversary of the birth of Bernhard Riemann – the German pioneer behind one of the field’s greatest unsolved problems. item.description: Photographs showing weathered and peeling radar-absorbing coatings on the US Air Force’s F-22 Raptor have repeatedly raised concerns in recent years. Photographs circulating online have also been presented as evidence of how surface damage could compromise the stealth fighter’s ability to evade radar detection. item.title: SCMP: How is the PLA countering small FPV drones and their swarms?
item.description: Small multirotor and first-person view drones are now widely used – and one of the most challenging new threats – on the modern battlefield. These drones are small, they fly at low altitudes usually off the traditional air defence radars, and combined with their manoeuvrability they are difficult to detect. A camera on an FPV drone gives the operator a live video feed that can be viewed through goggles, a headset or screen. These drones can be used for precision strikes against personnel,...

item.description: China has narrowed its power gap with the US in Asia to a record low, largely due to Washington’s own “missteps”, according to an Australian think tank’s annual gauge. The 2026 edition of the Lowy Institute’s Asia Power Index, released on Sunday, painted a picture of an “increasingly contested regional balance of power”.
